title: Practice Test 4
description: A full-length adaptive digital SAT practice test written by SAT Ustoz: 98 questions, two modules per section, with an explanation for every question.

questions.passage: Farmers in southern Spain often plant pomegranate orchards on sheltered, sunny slopes because the young trees are ______ to frost: a single cold night in early spring can destroy a whole season's blossoms.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: One cold night can destroy the blossoms, so the trees are easily harmed by frost, or **vulnerable** to it. *Resistant* is the opposite.

questions.passage: Early portrait photographers needed exposures lasting several seconds, so their sitters had to remain ______ in front of the camera; even a slight turn of the head left the face blurred in the finished picture.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Any movement blurred the face, so sitters had to stay completely still, or **immobile**. Sitting *upright* does not stop a person from turning their head.

questions.passage: Recording speakers in a few mountain villages in northern Italy, linguist Giulia Romano found that the oldest residents still use several verb endings that have ______ from the standard language: younger villagers, like speakers elsewhere in the country, no longer use them at all.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Endings that no one else uses anymore have disappeared, or **vanished**, from the standard language. *Emerged* would mean they had newly appeared.

questions.passage: Archivist Martin Hughes warns that the handwritten notes on the backs of old studio photographs are not always ______ guides to who appears in them: many were added decades later by relatives who were guessing at names and dates.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: The blank names a quality the notes often lack. Guesses added decades later cannot be trusted as expert sources, so the notes are not always **authoritative**. *Conjectural* describes the guesses themselves, so "not always conjectural" says the opposite of what the text means.

questions.passage: Public health researchers often find it hard to tell whether a new clinic improves a community's health or simply opens in places where people were already healthier. To get around this problem, epidemiologist Grace Mwangi studied a program that used a lottery to decide which of 60 villages would receive clinics first, and she compared the winners with the villages that had not yet won. __Because chance alone decided which villages got clinics, any later difference in health between the two groups could be credited to the clinics themselves.__
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It explains why the approach described in the previous sentence addresses the problem identified in the first sentence.
It presents a result that contradicts Mwangi's expectations about the clinics.
It describes a weakness of the lottery that the program used.
It introduces a second problem that the study was not designed to solve.
questions.explanation: The first sentence names a problem (healthier places might get clinics), and the underlined sentence explains why a lottery solves it: chance, not health, chose the villages.

questions.passage: At a ruined fortress in the desert of southern Egypt, archaeologists uncovered hundreds of clay jars closed with stamped clay stoppers. The excavation team first assumed that each stamp identified the household that owned a jar. Archaeologist Samuel Ortiz noticed, however, that jars holding the same kind of grain carried the same stamp no matter where in the fortress they were stored. He now argues that the stamps recorded what each jar contained, working less like signatures than like labels.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that the fortress was used mainly to store grain rather than to defend the region
To describe the methods archaeologists use to determine the age of clay jars
To explain how an observation led a researcher to reinterpret the purpose of markings on ancient objects
To show that later evidence confirmed the excavation team's first assumption about the stamps
questions.explanation: The text moves from the team's first assumption to Ortiz's observation and his new reading of the stamps. Grain storage is only a detail, not the point, and the observation overturns the first assumption rather than confirming it.

questions.passage:
**Text 1**
Some commentators argue that text messaging is damaging young people's writing. They point to the abbreviations, missing punctuation, and casual spellings found in messages and warn that habits formed on phones will inevitably spill over into school essays.

**Text 2**
Linguist Anneke de Vries collected essays and text messages written by the same 300 teenagers. The students used texting abbreviations constantly in their messages but almost never in their essays. Instead, they shifted styles to suit their audience, much as adults speak differently at a job interview than at a family dinner.
questions.prompt: Based on the texts, how would de Vries (Text 2) most likely respond to the commentators in Text 1?
choices: By agreeing that texting harms writing but arguing that the harm is limited to younger students
By arguing that the commentators assume students cannot keep different styles of writing separate, an assumption her findings do not support
By claiming that the abbreviations used in text messages improve the quality of students' essays
By recommending that teenagers be discouraged from using abbreviations in their text messages
questions.explanation: De Vries found that students kept texting style out of their essays, which undercuts the claim that phone habits "inevitably spill over." She shows no harm, but she also never says texting *improves* essays, so the choice about improving essays goes too far.

questions.passage: Many people assume that a tree builds its body mainly from material in the soil, but most of a tree's mass actually comes from the air. In photosynthesis, leaves take in carbon dioxide and use the energy of sunlight to make sugars, which the tree then turns into wood, bark, and new leaves. Water and minerals from the soil are essential, but they make up only a small share of a tree's dry weight.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Trees grow fastest in soil that is rich in minerals.
Photosynthesis takes place mainly in a tree's roots.
Most people correctly understand where a tree's mass comes from.
Although soil supplies needed water and minerals, most of the material in a tree comes from carbon dioxide in the air.
questions.explanation: The text corrects a common belief and explains that a tree's mass is built mostly from carbon dioxide, with soil playing a smaller role.

questions.passage:
The following text is from a short story. Elena has come back to her family's apricot orchard after several years of university in the city.

The trees were smaller than she remembered, their trunks knotted and gray, and the irrigation ditch that had seemed a river when she was six was now a step she crossed without noticing. But when her uncle handed her an apricot and she bit into it, the taste was exactly the same, so exactly the same that for a moment she was six again, barefoot on the warm bank.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Elena is disappointed to find that the orchard has been neglected since she left.
Although the orchard seems to have shrunk since her childhood, a familiar taste brings her early memories back with sudden force.
Elena realizes that she prefers life in the city to life in the orchard.
Elena's uncle tries to persuade her to stay and help with the harvest.
questions.explanation: Everything looks smaller to the grown Elena, but the unchanged taste of the apricot makes her feel six years old again. Nothing suggests the orchard was neglected; it is she who has changed.

questions.passage: Public health researcher Elif Demir hypothesizes that placing simple signs next to elevators in office buildings, encouraging people to use the stairs instead, leads more people to take the stairs.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Demir's hypothesis?
choices: In buildings where the signs were posted, the share of people taking the stairs rose from 12% to 19%, while it stayed the same in similar buildings without signs.
Most office workers surveyed said they would take the stairs more often if the stairs were closer to the entrance.
Buildings with more floors had fewer people taking the stairs than buildings with fewer floors.
People who regularly took the stairs reported higher fitness levels than people who used the elevator.
questions.explanation: This finding shows stair use rising where the signs went up but not in similar buildings without them, which links the increase to the signs.

questions.passage: Agronomist Diego Ramos claims that rows of mulberry trees planted along the edges of cotton fields reduce the harm done by hot, dry summer winds, because the trees slow the wind before it reaches the crop.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Ramos's claim?
choices: Mulberry leaves are used to feed silkworms, so farmers who plant the trees gain a second source of income.
During a summer of strong, dry winds, wind speeds inside fields bordered by mulberry trees were about 40% lower than inside unbordered fields, and the bordered fields showed far less wilting.
Farmers who plant mulberry trees tend to own larger fields than farmers who do not.
Cotton fields bordered by mulberry trees produced higher yields than unbordered fields in years with unusually heavy rain.
questions.explanation: This finding supports both parts of the claim: the trees slowed the wind, and the crop suffered less. Higher yields in *rainy* years say nothing about protection from hot, dry wind.

questions.passage: A researcher compared three irrigation methods on test plots of cotton on the Texas High Plains. She concludes that drip irrigation was the best choice of the three for farmers who want to save water without losing yield: ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
choices: furrow irrigation used 9,800 cubic meters of water per hectare.
sprinkler irrigation produced 3.0 tonnes per hectare, the lowest yield of the three methods.
drip irrigation used the least water of the three methods, 5,200 cubic meters per hectare, and also produced the highest yield, 3.3 tonnes per hectare.
drip irrigation used less water than sprinkler irrigation but produced a lower yield.
questions.explanation: Her conclusion needs drip irrigation to save water *and* keep yield. It used the least water (5,200) and had the highest yield (3.3). The choice saying drip had a lower yield misreads the table.

questions.passage: Archaeologists excavating a Bronze Age settlement found that nearly all of the animal bones in its oldest layers came from wild gazelles, while most bones in its later layers came from sheep and goats. The later layers also contained the remains of stone animal pens. These findings suggest that, over time, the settlement's residents ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: moved the settlement to a new location.
began hunting gazelles more often than before.
came to rely more on raising herd animals than on hunting wild ones.
questions.explanation: Bones shift from wild gazelles to sheep and goats, and pens appear, which points to a move from hunting toward herding.

questions.passage: In English, some of the most commonly used verbs, such as *be* and *go*, have irregular past-tense forms (*was*, *went*). Many verbs that were irregular centuries ago, however, now follow the regular *-ed* pattern; the old past tense of *help*, for example, was *holp*. Linguists explain this pattern by noting that learners must hear an irregular form many times to remember it. When a learner has rarely heard a verb's irregular form, the learner tends to apply the regular rule instead. If this explanation is correct, then ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: among verbs that are irregular today, those used least often are the most likely to become regular in the future.
the most commonly used verbs are the most likely to lose their irregular forms.
learners find irregular verb forms easier to remember than regular ones.
every verb that is regular today was irregular at some earlier time.
questions.explanation: Rare irregular forms are heard too seldom to be remembered, so they are the ones that get replaced by the regular rule. The choice about the most common verbs reverses this: frequent use *protects* irregular forms. The choice about every regular verb overgeneralizes from "many verbs."

questions.passage: Many photographers prefer to work in the hour after sunrise. At that time, the Sun is low in the sky, and its light passes through more of the ______ the light that reaches the camera looks warmer and softer than it does at midday.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Both parts are complete sentences, so a semicolon joins them. A comma alone makes a comma splice, and no punctuation makes a run-on.

questions.passage: Photographer Hana Kobayashi's best-known ______ a series of portraits of beekeepers in the Carpathian Mountains, took her nearly four years to complete.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "A series of portraits... Mountains" renames the project and closes with a comma, so it must open with a comma too.

questions.passage: The rice ______ farmers in the river delta have planted for generations tolerates salty soil better than most modern varieties do.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "That farmers... generations" identifies which variety is meant, so it is essential and takes no punctuation. A semicolon or colon would split the subject from its verb, "tolerates."

questions.passage: The charred grains of barley and wheat recovered from storage pits beneath the floor of the ancient ______ suggest that the settlement's residents grew both crops.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Everything from "The charred grains" to "house" is the subject, and "suggest" is its verb. No punctuation should separate a subject from its verb, however long the subject is.

questions.passage: The photographs in the exhibition, all taken in Marrakesh's markets during the 1970s, ______ traders, shoppers, and craftspeople at work.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is the plural "photographs," so the verb is **show**. The phrase between the commas does not change the subject.

questions.passage: Linguists who record endangered languages work closely with community members, since the speakers themselves understand best how ______ language is used in everyday life.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The pronoun refers to the plural "speakers," so the possessive is **their**. *They're* means "they are," and *there* names a place.

questions.passage: Tea plants grown on high mountain slopes, where cool temperatures slow their growth and thin air exposes them to stronger sunlight, ______ leaves with unusually concentrated flavors.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject "Tea plants" needs a main verb, and the long "where" clause hides that fact. Only **produce** is a complete verb; the other choices leave the sentence without one.

questions.passage: Potatoes can be grown from pieces of the potato itself rather than from seeds. ______ farmers often set aside part of one year's harvest to plant the following spring.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Saving potatoes to plant is a result of the fact that potatoes grow from pieces of potato, so **Therefore** fits.

questions.passage: Photographers using film often had to wait days to learn whether a picture had come out, since the film first had to be developed in a darkroom. ______ digital cameras display each image within a second of its being taken.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The waiting of the film era is set against the instant display of digital cameras, so a contrast is needed.

questions.passage: Over its long history, the English language has absorbed words from many other languages. ______ the everyday word *sofa* can be traced back to Arabic, and *tea* comes from Chinese.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The two words are examples of words English has absorbed, so **For instance** fits.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Oral rehydration solution (ORS) is a mixture of clean water, salts, and sugar.
• It is used to treat dehydration caused by diarrhea.
• The sugar helps the intestines absorb the salts, and water follows the salts into the body.
• ORS is cheap to prepare and can be given at home without special equipment.
questions.prompt: The student wants to explain why ORS is practical for families who live far from a hospital. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Oral rehydration solution is a mixture of clean water, salts, and sugar.
Because it is cheap to prepare and can be given at home without special equipment, oral rehydration solution is practical even for families far from a hospital.
In oral rehydration solution, sugar helps the intestines absorb salts, and water follows the salts into the body.
Oral rehydration solution is used to treat dehydration caused by diarrhea.
questions.explanation: Families far from a hospital need a treatment they can afford and give at home. Only this choice gives those reasons.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Marta Jiménez is a photographer from Seville.
• In 1978, she photographed the same street in Seville's old city every morning for a year.
• In 2018, she returned and photographed the street every morning for another year.
• An exhibition in Madrid displayed photographs from the two years side by side.
questions.prompt: The student wants to emphasize how long a span of time Jiménez's project covers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Jiménez is a photographer from Seville.
An exhibition in Madrid displayed Jiménez's photographs from two different years side by side.
In 1978, Jiménez photographed the same street in Seville's old city every morning for a year.
Jiménez's project spans four decades: she photographed the same Seville street every morning in 1978 and again in 2018.
questions.explanation: Only this choice gives both years, which shows that the project stretches across forty years.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Linguist Marta Kowalczyk taught a made-up language to two groups of volunteers.
• In Group 1, every volunteer learned the language directly from Kowalczyk.
• In Group 2, each volunteer learned the language from the volunteer before them, forming a chain of ten "generations."
• By the end, Group 2's version of the language had become much more regular, with words following more consistent patterns.
• Group 1's version had changed very little.
• Kowalczyk concluded that being passed between many learners may help explain why languages become more regular over time.
questions.prompt: The student wants to present Kowalczyk's conclusion along with the finding that supports it. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Because the made-up language became much more regular only when it was passed along a chain of learners, Kowalczyk concluded that being passed between many learners may help explain why languages grow more regular over time.
Kowalczyk concluded that being passed between many learners may help explain why languages become more regular over time.
In Kowalczyk's study, Group 2's version of the language became much more regular, while Group 1's version changed very little.
Kowalczyk taught a made-up language to two groups: one learned it directly from her, and the other learned it along a chain of ten volunteers.
questions.explanation: The goal has two parts. One choice gives only the conclusion and another gives only the finding; only the correct choice connects the finding to the conclusion it supports.

questions.passage: The school's new greenhouse lets students grow vegetables even in January, when the ground outside is too ______ for planting.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Ground in January that cannot be planted is hard with cold, or **frozen**, which is why a greenhouse is needed.

questions.passage: The old map in the village library was so ______ that the hikers could no longer read the names of the mountain passes printed on it.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Printing that can no longer be read has lost its color with age, so the map was **faded**.

questions.passage: The district's vaccination campaign was ______: within six months, nearly every child in the district had received the vaccine.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Reaching nearly every child means the campaign achieved its goal, so it was **successful**.

questions.passage: Words can change their meanings slowly over time. The English word *nice*, for example, once meant "foolish," and its meaning ______ gradually over several centuries before it came to mean "pleasant."
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: A meaning that moved from "foolish" to "pleasant" changed, or **shifted**. It did not *vanish*, because the word still has a meaning.

questions.passage: Archaeologists sometimes use drones to photograph sites from above. From the air, small differences in the color of crops or soil can reveal the outlines of buried walls and ditches that cannot be seen by someone walking across the same field.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To explain how photographs taken from above can help archaeologists find buried structures
To describe how farmers decide which crops to plant near ancient sites
To compare two kinds of drones that archaeologists use
To argue that drones are too expensive for most archaeologists to use
questions.explanation: The text describes what aerial photographs reveal: the outlines of buried walls and ditches.

questions.passage: Sunflowers are often said to follow the Sun across the sky. In fact, only young sunflowers do this: during the day their flower heads turn from east to west, and at night they swing back to face east. __Once the plants mature, the heads stop moving and stay facing east.__ Researchers have found that east-facing flowers warm up faster in the morning and attract more bees.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It explains why young sunflowers turn their heads during the day.
It describes what happens to the flower heads after the stage described in the previous sentence.
It presents evidence that contradicts the researchers' findings about bees.
It introduces a disagreement among researchers about how sunflowers behave.
questions.explanation: The previous sentence describes young plants; the underlined sentence tells what the heads do once the plants are mature.

questions.passage:
**Text 1**
Many home gardeners believe that plants grow best when they are watered a little every day, since daily watering keeps the soil from ever drying out.

**Text 2**
Horticulturist Peter Lang grew pepper plants under two watering plans. Plants watered deeply twice a week grew deeper roots and survived a dry spell better than plants given a small amount of water every day. Deep, infrequent watering, Lang explains, encourages roots to grow down toward the moisture stored deeper in the soil.
questions.prompt: Based on the texts, how would Lang (Text 2) most likely respond to the gardeners' belief in Text 1?
choices: By arguing that watering a little every day may keep roots shallow and leave plants less able to survive dry periods
By agreeing that the soil around plants should never be allowed to dry out
By claiming that pepper plants need more water than most garden plants
By suggesting that gardeners should stop watering their plants entirely
questions.explanation: Lang found that deep, infrequent watering produced deeper roots and better survival, so he would question the daily-watering habit.

questions.passage: Long before photography was invented, artists used a device called a camera obscura. It was a dark box or room with a small hole in one wall. Light passing through the hole projected an upside-down image of the scene outside onto the opposite wall, and artists could trace that image to draw accurately. The same principle, light passing through a small opening to form an image, is at work inside every modern camera.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Artists who traced images were less skilled than artists who did not.
The camera obscura, an early device that used a small opening to form images, works on the same principle as modern cameras.
The camera obscura was invented soon after the first photographs were taken.
questions.explanation: The text explains how the camera obscura worked and ends by linking it to modern cameras.

questions.passage: In 1854, an outbreak of cholera killed hundreds of people in one London neighborhood. Many doctors at the time believed that the disease spread through foul-smelling air. Physician John Snow instead traced where each victim had lived and found that the deaths were clustered around a single public water pump. His investigation persuaded local officials to remove the pump's handle and pointed toward the now-accepted view that cholera spreads through contaminated water.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: By tracing where the victims had lived, Snow found evidence that the outbreak was linked to a water source rather than to bad air.
Most doctors in the 1850s agreed with Snow about how cholera spread.
The outbreak of 1854 was the deadliest in London's history.
Removing the pump's handle had no effect on the outbreak.
questions.explanation: The text centers on Snow's investigation, which tied the deaths to a pump and challenged the belief that bad air spread the disease.

questions.passage: A gardener hypothesizes that mixing used coffee grounds into the soil helps her basil plants grow taller.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support the gardener's hypothesis?
choices: Basil grows best in sunny places.
Many cafés throw away large amounts of coffee grounds every day.
Several of her neighbors also add coffee grounds to their gardens.
Basil plants grown in soil mixed with coffee grounds grew taller, on average, than identical plants grown in the same soil without coffee grounds.
questions.explanation: Only this finding compares plants with and without coffee grounds and shows the taller growth she predicted.

questions.passage: Linguist Sophie Tremblay hypothesizes that people in Montreal who speak both French and English switch to English more often when talking about technology than when talking about family.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Tremblay's hypothesis?
choices: Most of the speakers she recorded learned French before they learned English.
In recorded conversations, speakers used English in about 60% of their sentences about computers and phones but in only about 15% of their sentences about relatives.
Speakers switched languages more often when talking with friends than when talking with strangers.
Many of the speakers said that they enjoy talking about new technology.
questions.explanation: This finding compares the two topics directly and shows much more English in talk about technology. The choice about friends and strangers concerns the listener, not the topic.

questions.passage: A school nurse recorded how many students in each grade received a flu vaccine at the school clinic. According to her records, the grade with the most vaccinated students was ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?
questions.explanation: 142 is the largest number in the table, and it belongs to grade 10.

questions.passage: Snow leopards live in the high mountains of the Himalayas, where they hunt wild sheep and goats on steep, rocky slopes. Their long, thick tails help them keep their balance as they leap from ledge to ledge. Without such tails, snow leopards would likely ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: prefer to live in flat grasslands.
have more difficulty moving safely across steep, rocky ground.
grow thicker fur to stay warm.
questions.explanation: The tail helps with balance on ledges, so without it the leopards would find steep ground harder to cross.

questions.passage: Archaeologists studying an ancient town found coins from at least six different kingdoms buried beneath the floor of its central market. None of the kingdoms that made the coins was located within 300 kilometers of the town. These findings suggest that the town's market ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: was used only by farmers from the surrounding villages.
was built after the town had been abandoned.
did not use coins for buying and selling.
was visited by traders who had traveled long distances.
questions.explanation: Coins from many faraway kingdoms most likely arrived with people who came from far away to trade.

questions.passage: When the photographer finally developed her ______ she discovered that half of the pictures from her trip were blank.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: A comma separates the introductory "When..." clause from the main sentence. A semicolon or colon would need a complete sentence before it.

questions.passage: The school garden's first harvest included three ______ radishes, spinach, and green onions.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: A colon introduces a list after a complete sentence. A semicolon would need a complete sentence after it.

questions.passage: The ______ a high-speed train that links Tokyo with Nagoya and Osaka, can travel at more than 250 kilometers per hour.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "A high-speed train... Osaka" renames the Nozomi and closes with a comma, so it must open with a comma too.

questions.passage: Clay tablets can survive for thousands of years if they are kept dry. Tablets that are exposed to ______ slowly crumble.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "However" interrupts a single sentence here, so it needs a comma on each side. A semicolon would need a complete sentence before it, and "Tablets that are exposed to water" is not one.

questions.passage: Last spring, the school photography club ______ an exhibition of its members' work in the main hall.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Last spring" places the event in the past, so the past tense **held** is needed.

questions.passage: The roots of the licorice plant, which grows wild along rivers in southern Europe, ______ used to sweeten teas and medicines.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is the plural "roots," not "plant," so the verb is **are**.

questions.passage: The three ______ reports showed that vaccination rates had risen in every district of the region.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The reports belong to three nurses, a plural noun ending in *s*, so the possessive is **nurses'**.

questions.passage: Winter wheat must go through a period of cold weather before it can produce grain. ______ farmers in Kansas plant it in autumn, so that the young plants pass the winter in the fields and are ready to harvest in early summer.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Farmers plant in autumn *because* the wheat needs cold weather, so **For this reason** fits.

questions.passage: A camera can record a whole landscape in a fraction of a second. ______ a painter might spend weeks or even months on a single landscape.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: The painter's weeks are set against the camera's fraction of a second, so the sentences are being compared and contrasted.

questions.passage: Archaeologists usually dig with small hand tools, removing soil only a few centimeters at a time. ______ they record the exact position of every object before lifting it out of the ground.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Recording each object's position is another careful practice added to digging slowly, so **In addition** fits.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• A camera trap is a camera that takes a photograph automatically when an animal moves in front of it.
• Camera traps can be left in place for weeks at a time.
• Researchers use them to study shy or nocturnal animals.
• Some camera traps use infrared light instead of a visible flash.
questions.prompt: The student wants to explain why camera traps are useful for studying shy animals. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Some camera traps use infrared light instead of a visible flash.
Camera traps can be left in place for weeks at a time.
Because camera traps photograph animals automatically and can be left in place for weeks, they let researchers study shy or nocturnal animals.
A camera trap is a camera that takes a photograph automatically when an animal moves in front of it.
questions.explanation: Only this choice connects what camera traps do to the goal of studying shy animals. The other choices give single facts without saying why they help.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Archaeologist Sarah Klein studied two ancient pottery workshops in the Nile Valley.
• The first workshop was active about 2,300 years ago.
• The second workshop was active about 1,100 years ago.
• Both workshops made bowls decorated with the same wave-shaped pattern.
questions.prompt: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two workshops. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The first workshop Klein studied was active about 2,300 years ago.
The two workshops Klein studied were active about 1,200 years apart.
Klein studied two ancient pottery workshops in the Nile Valley.
Although they were active more than a thousand years apart, both workshops made bowls decorated with the same wave-shaped pattern.
questions.explanation: The shared wave pattern is the similarity. The choice about the 1,200-year gap stresses a difference instead.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• A city added drinking fountains to 40 of its parks.
• Before the change, a survey found that 30% of park visitors brought sugary drinks with them.
• A year after the fountains were added, 18% of visitors did.
• The city plans to add fountains to 25 more parks.
questions.prompt: The student wants to present what changed after the fountains were added. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The city plans to add drinking fountains to 25 more parks.
After the city added drinking fountains to 40 parks, the share of park visitors bringing sugary drinks fell from 30% to 18%.
A survey found that 30% of park visitors brought sugary drinks with them.
A city added drinking fountains to 40 of its parks.
questions.explanation: Only this choice gives the before and after figures that show the change.

questions.passage: Botanist Ingrid Solberg's account of how the saltbush survives long droughts is deliberately ______: she describes the three mechanisms that her measurements clearly support and declines to speculate about a fourth that other researchers have proposed.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Sticking to what the evidence supports and refusing to speculate is cautious, or **circumspect**. The account leaves out a proposed fourth mechanism, so it is not *exhaustive*, and refusing to speculate is the opposite of *speculative*.

questions.passage: Many viewers assume that a documentary photograph simply records whatever was in front of the camera, but photographer Tavita Leota insists that every such image is ______: the photographer chooses where to stand, what to leave outside the frame, and which instant to capture.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Leota lists the choices that shape every image, so each photograph is built, or **constructed**. *Fraudulent* goes too far: making choices is not the same as deceiving viewers.

questions.passage: The editors of the new Spanish dictionary describe their approach as ______ rather than prescriptive: they aim to record how people actually use words today, not to rule on how words ought to be used.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Recording actual usage instead of setting rules is a **descriptive** approach, the opposite of *prescriptive*. *Authoritative* and *corrective* both suggest ruling on correct usage, which the editors reject.

questions.passage: Far from settling the debate over the settlement's age, the new radiocarbon dates have proved ______: samples taken from the same layer returned results more than four centuries apart, lending some support to both competing timelines.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
questions.explanation: Results that support both sides are open to more than one reading, or **equivocal**. *Decisive* is the opposite, as "Far from settling the debate" signals.

questions.passage: For decades, campaigns to reduce the amount of salt people eat focused on persuading individuals to stop adding salt to their food at the table. __Yet in many countries, most of the salt in people's diets is already in their food when they buy it, added during the making of bread, sauces, and packaged meals.__ Some researchers therefore argue that working with food producers to lower salt levels gradually, by amounts too small for shoppers to notice, would do more for public health than any warning label.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
choices: It gives an example of a campaign that succeeded in changing individual behavior.
It presents a fact suggesting that the approach described in the first sentence addresses only a small part of the problem.
It describes a method food producers have used to make reductions in salt unnoticeable.
It explains why shoppers tend to ignore warnings about the health effects of salt.
questions.explanation: If most salt is added before food is bought, campaigns about the salt shaker miss most of it. The underlined sentence mentions food production, but the unnoticeable reductions are only *proposed* later, not described as a method already in use.

questions.passage:
The following text is from a short story. Lucas, a young photographer, is printing pictures of his grandmother.

For weeks he had photographed her in the courtyard, and in every picture she wore the same polite, careful smile she gave to visitors. Lucas had nearly given up when, on the last frame of the roll, he found an image he did not remember taking: his grandmother turned half away, laughing at something outside the frame, one hand raised against the sun. He held the wet print under the red darkroom light for a long time. It was the only one that looked like her.
questions.prompt: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes a character's growing frustration and then his decision to abandon a project.
It contrasts two photographers' approaches to the same subject.
It recalls an event from a character's childhood and then explains why he regrets it.
It describes repeated attempts that fall short and then an unexpected result that succeeds.
questions.explanation: Weeks of stiff, posed pictures are followed by one unplanned image that finally captures her. Lucas *nearly* gives up but does not, so the choice about abandoning the project misreads the ending.

questions.passage:
**Text 1**
Many archaeologists have held that farming spread across North Africa from a single early center: as farming communities grew, they moved into new land and carried their crops with them.

**Text 2**
A team led by geneticist Laila Mansour analyzed ancient grains from twelve sites in the region. At several sites, the earliest barley was most closely related to the wild barley that still grows nearby, suggesting that it was domesticated locally. At the same sites, however, the earliest wheat was genetically almost identical to wheat from distant early farming centers.
questions.prompt: Based on the texts, how would Mansour's team (Text 2) most likely respond to the view described in Text 1?
choices: By rejecting the idea that any crop arrived in the region from elsewhere
By agreeing that the view in Text 1 fully explains how farming spread in the region
By suggesting that the view may be accurate for some crops but does not account for the local domestication of others
By arguing that wheat, rather than barley, was the first crop grown in the region
questions.explanation: The wheat fits the idea of crops arriving from elsewhere, but the barley was domesticated locally. Rejecting all outside crops ignores the wheat evidence, and nothing in Text 2 says which crop came first.

questions.passage: When speakers of two languages live side by side for generations, each language often borrows words from the other. Linguist Erik Johansson argues, however, that borrowed words tell only part of the story. In the bilingual towns he studied, the two languages had also come to arrange words in sentences in increasingly similar ways, even though speakers rarely noticed the change and continued to think of the languages as entirely separate.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Johansson argues that long contact between two languages can change not only their vocabulary but also their sentence structure, often without speakers being aware of it.
Johansson found that speakers in bilingual towns borrow fewer words than linguists had assumed.
Speakers in the bilingual towns Johansson studied regard the two languages as a single language.
Johansson argues that borrowed words are the most reliable evidence that two languages have been in contact.
questions.explanation: Johansson goes beyond borrowed words to show changes in word order that speakers did not notice. He never says fewer words were borrowed, and the speakers still see the languages as separate.

questions.passage:
The following text is from a poem. The speaker describes a wheat field after the harvest.

The stubble stands in rows of pale gold wire,
the reapers gone, the swallows flown away.
The field that fed the village through the year
lies bare beneath the low October sky,
and yet it does not look to me like loss:
it rests the way an open hand will rest
that has given all it held, and does not doubt
that spring will fill it, as it always has.
questions.prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: The speaker mourns the departure of the workers who harvested the field.
The speaker worries that the village will not have enough food in the coming year.
The speaker describes how the swallows help the field recover after the harvest.
The speaker sees the harvested field as resting rather than lost, trusting that it will be productive again.
questions.explanation: The speaker says the bare field "does not look to me like loss" and compares it to an open hand that expects spring to fill it again. The departed reapers are a detail, not the focus.

questions.passage: Botanist Priya Raman has proposed that a mountain gentian closes its flowers before afternoon storms in response to the drop in air temperature that usually comes before the rain, not in response to the darkening of the sky.
questions.prompt: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Raman's proposal?
choices: On most afternoons, the temperature and the light level fell at about the same time before storms arrived.
In a greenhouse, the flowers closed within minutes when the light was dimmed while the temperature was held steady, but they stayed open when the temperature was lowered under bright light.
Flowers that were prevented from closing before storms produced fewer seeds than flowers that closed normally.
The gentian grows mainly at elevations where afternoon storms are common.
questions.explanation: This experiment separates the two possible triggers: dimming alone closed the flowers, while cooling alone did not, which is the opposite of Raman's proposal. A finding in which light and temperature fall together cannot tell the triggers apart.

questions.passage: A health department tracked the share of two-year-olds vaccinated against measles in four districts. An official claims that the gap between the best- and worst-performing districts narrowed between 2019 and 2023 but did not disappear. ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the official's claim?
choices: District B's rate rose by 12 percentage points, more than any other district's rate rose.
Every district's vaccination rate was higher in 2023 than in 2019.
In 2023, District C's rate of 93% was only 1 percentage point below District A's rate.
In 2019, rates ranged from 78% in District B to 91% in District A, while in 2023 they ranged from 86% in District D to 94% in District A.
questions.explanation: The claim is about the gap between the highest and lowest rates. That gap was 91 − 78 = 13 points in 2019 and 94 − 86 = 8 points in 2023: smaller, but not zero. The other choices are true but say nothing about that gap.

questions.passage: Agronomists compared three wheat varieties over a normal year and a drought year. One agronomist argues that a farmer who expects frequent droughts should choose Sterling, even though it is not the highest-yielding variety in a normal year. ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support the agronomist's argument?
choices: Sterling's yield fell by only 1.3 tonnes per hectare in the drought year, far less than the other two varieties' yields fell, leaving Sterling with the highest yield of the three in that year.
Aurora produced the highest yield of the three varieties in the normal year, 6.2 tonnes per hectare.
Crystal's yield in the drought year, 3.3 tonnes per hectare, was higher than Aurora's.
All three varieties produced less wheat in the drought year than in the normal year.
questions.explanation: Sterling dropped from 5.4 to 4.1 (1.3 tonnes), while Aurora dropped 3.3 and Crystal 2.6, so Sterling did best in the drought. The other choices are accurate but do not show that Sterling is the better choice when droughts are common.
