questions.passage: Many desert plants open the pores on their leaves, called stomata, only at night, when cooler air means that less water evaporates through them. The plants take in carbon dioxide through the open stomata and store it chemically until daylight, when they use it in photosynthesis. This strategy greatly reduces water loss, but a plant can store only a limited amount of carbon dioxide overnight. Compared with plants in well-watered places that keep their stomata open during the day, these desert plants are therefore likely to ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: lose more water through their leaves.
carry out photosynthesis only at night.
take in carbon dioxide mainly during the hottest hours of the day.
grow more slowly, since the carbon dioxide available to them for photosynthesis is limited.
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis needs carbon dioxide, and these plants have only what they stored overnight, so they can build less and grow more slowly. They take in carbon dioxide at night but photosynthesize in daylight, so the choice saying they photosynthesize only at night confuses the two steps.

questions.passage: Most photographic plates used before the 1880s responded strongly to blue light but barely responded to red light. In the finished photographs, objects that reflected a great deal of blue light therefore appeared pale, while red objects appeared nearly black. A historian studying an 1860s portrait in which a woman wears a very dark dress should therefore conclude that the dress ______
questions.prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?
choices: may have been red, since red fabric would also have looked nearly black in the photograph.
was probably blue, since blue was a common color for dresses at the time.
must have been pale, since the plates reversed light and dark areas.
questions.explanation: Because red also appeared nearly black, a dark dress could have been red, so the historian cannot assume black. A blue dress would have looked pale, not dark.

questions.passage: The three writing systems used in modern Japanese ______ hiragana, katakana, and kanji.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: A colon or dash must follow a complete sentence, and "The three writing systems... are" is not one: the verb still needs its complement. No punctuation belongs between a verb and what completes it.

questions.passage: Award-winning ______ Asante spent two years photographing fishing families on the shores of Lake Malawi.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Award-winning photographer" works like a title in front of the name, and the name is needed to say which photographer is meant, so no punctuation goes between them. A single comma, semicolon, or colon would split the subject apart.

questions.passage: The seeds of some desert ______ each smaller than a grain of sand, can lie in the soil for decades, waiting for a rare heavy rain.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: "Each smaller than a grain of sand" is extra information that closes with a comma, so it must open with a comma. A dash would need a matching dash at the end.

questions.passage: After years of testing, the restorers finally identified the source of the mural's deep blue ______ lapis lazuli, ground by hand and mixed with plant gum.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: What follows names the pigment, so a colon introduces it. A semicolon would need a complete sentence after it, and "lapis lazuli, ground... gum" is only a phrase.

questions.passage: The archive's collection of glass-plate negatives, some of which show streets in Vienna that no longer exist, ______ being digitized so that researchers can study it online.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular "collection," not "negatives" or "streets," so the verb is **is**. The singular "it" at the end confirms this.

questions.passage: Sorting more than 20,000 pottery fragments by color, thickness, and decoration, ______
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: the team showed that the settlement had traded with at least five distant regions.
the settlement was shown by the team to have traded with at least five distant regions.
at least five distant regions were shown by the team to have traded with the settlement.
it was shown by the team that the settlement had traded with at least five distant regions.
questions.explanation: The opening phrase describes whoever did the sorting, so "the team" must come right after the comma. The settlement and the regions did not sort anything.

questions.passage: In 1998, linguist Ellen Brooks traveled to three mountain villages, recorded the speech of their oldest residents, and ______ that many of them used words unknown to younger speakers.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The three actions form a series in the past ("traveled," "recorded"), so the last verb must match: **noted**.

questions.passage: Several crops that originated in the Americas, including tomatoes and peppers, were unknown in Europe until about five hundred years ago. ______ they are now so central to Italian and Hungarian cooking that many people assume they have always been grown there.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Being recent arrivals did not stop these crops from becoming central to the cuisine, so a contrast is needed. *Consequently* is wrong because being unknown did not *cause* them to become common.

questions.passage: Infrared photography records light that human eyes cannot see. Healthy leaves reflect a great deal of infrared light, so in infrared photographs they appear bright white. ______ leaves that are diseased or short of water reflect less infrared light and appear darker, which lets farmers spot struggling plants from the air before any damage is visible to the eye.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Unhealthy leaves do the reverse of healthy ones (less reflection, darker image), so **Conversely** fits. *Likewise* would signal the same behavior.

questions.passage: In normal years, the new wheat variety yields about 10% less grain than the variety most farmers now plant. ______ farmers in drought-prone districts have begun planting it widely, because in dry years it can produce nearly twice as much grain.
questions.prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
questions.explanation: Farmers adopt the variety despite its lower normal-year yield, so a concession is needed. The lower yield is not a cause of its popularity, which rules out *As a result*.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• The daguerreotype, introduced in 1839, produced a single, highly detailed image on a polished metal plate.
• A daguerreotype image could not be copied.
• The calotype, introduced in 1841, produced a negative on paper.
• Any number of paper prints could be made from one calotype negative.
• Calotype prints were less sharp than daguerreotypes.
questions.prompt: The student wants to emphasize a disadvantage of the calotype compared with the daguerreotype. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Unlike a daguerreotype, which could not be copied, a calotype negative could be used to make any number of prints.
The daguerreotype was introduced in 1839, two years before the calotype.
The daguerreotype and the calotype were both early photographic processes that produced images.
Although a calotype negative could be used to make many prints, those prints were less sharp than the highly detailed images a daguerreotype produced.
questions.explanation: The goal is a *disadvantage* of the calotype: its prints were less sharp. The choice about copying compares the two processes but gives the calotype's advantage instead.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Researchers wanted to find out whether text-message reminders help children receive their second measles vaccine dose on time.
• They randomly assigned 1,200 families either to receive reminders or to receive no reminders.
• In the reminder group, 84% of children received the dose on time.
• In the group without reminders, 71% of children did.
questions.prompt: The student wants to describe the study's aim and method without revealing its results. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Children whose families received text-message reminders were more likely to get their second measles dose on time: 84% did, compared with 71% of other children.
Researchers wanted to know whether text-message reminders help children get their second measles dose on time.
To learn whether text-message reminders help children get their second measles dose on time, researchers randomly assigned 1,200 families to receive reminders or no reminders.
After 1,200 families were randomly assigned to two groups, 84% of the children in the reminder group got their second measles dose on time.
questions.explanation: The choice must give both the aim and the method and leave out the results. The choice that states only the aim leaves out the method, and the choices with percentages reveal results.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

• Harrowfield is an archaeological site in northern England.
• Excavations there began in 2016.
• Archaeologists found a workshop containing glass beads at every stage of production.
• The glass was made from local sand.
• Before this discovery, archaeologists believed that all the glass beads found in the region had been imported.
questions.prompt: The student wants to explain why the discovery at Harrowfield changed archaeologists' understanding of the region. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Harrowfield's workshop, where glass beads were made from local sand, overturned archaeologists' earlier belief that all of the region's glass beads had been imported.
Excavations at Harrowfield, an archaeological site in northern England, began in 2016.
At Harrowfield, archaeologists found a workshop containing glass beads at every stage of production.
Archaeologists once believed that all of the glass beads found in the region had been imported.
questions.explanation: Explaining a change in understanding needs both the old belief and the new evidence that overturned it. The choice about the workshop gives only the find, and the choice about imports gives only the old belief.

questions.prompt: A gardener planted 96 tulip bulbs. She planted the same number of bulbs in each of 7 rows and planted the remaining 12 bulbs along a path. How many bulbs did she plant in each row?
questions.explanation: If each row has $x$ bulbs, then $7x + 12 = 96$. Subtract 12: $7x = 84$, so $x = 12$. 84 is the total in all 7 rows.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.prompt: A machine at a bakery shapes 84 loaves of bread in 4 minutes. At this rate, how many loaves will the machine shape in 9 minutes?
questions.explanation: The machine shapes $84 \div 4 = 21$ loaves per minute, and $21 \times 9 = 189$.

questions.prompt: The function $g$ is defined by $g(t) = \dfrac{t}{2} - 9$. What is the value of $g(-6)$?
Which expression is equivalent to $8m - 3(2m - 5)$?
questions.explanation: Distribute the $-3$ to both terms: $8m - 6m + 15 = 2m + 15$. Writing $-15$ forgets that $-3 \times -5 = 15$.

questions.prompt: After a 20% discount, the price of a phone is \$250. What was the price of the phone, in dollars, before the discount?
questions.explanation: The sale price is 80% of the original price: $0.80p = 250$, so $p = 312.50$. Adding 20% of \$250 gives 300, but the 20% was taken from the original price, not from \$250.

questions.skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
questions.prompt: $$5p + 2q = 31$$ $$p - 2q = -1$$ If $(p, q)$ is the solution to the given system of equations, what is the value of $p + q$?
questions.explanation: Adding the equations eliminates $q$: $6p = 30$, so $p = 5$. Then $5 - 2q = -1$ gives $q = 3$, and $p + q = 8$.

questions.prompt: A line in the $xy$-plane passes through the points $(-2, 5)$ and $(4, -7)$. What is the slope of the line?
In triangle $PQR$, the measure of angle $Q$ is $20^\circ$ greater than the measure of angle $P$, and the measure of angle $R$ is 3 times the measure of angle $P$. What is the measure of angle $R$?
questions.explanation: Let angle $P$ be $p$ degrees. Then $p + (p + 20) + 3p = 180$, so $5p = 160$ and $p = 32$. Angle $R$ is $3(32) = 96$ degrees; 32 and 52 are angles $P$ and $Q$.

questions.prompt: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = (x - 4)(x + 2)$. For what value of $x$ does $f(x)$ reach its minimum value?
questions.explanation: The zeros are 4 and $-2$, and a parabola's vertex lies halfway between its zeros: $\dfrac{4 + (-2)}{2} = 1$. The minimum value itself is $f(1) = -9$, but the question asks for $x$.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.prompt: The data set $12, 15, 15, 18, 20$ is changed by replacing the value 20 with 35. Which statement describes how the mean and the median of the data set change?
choices: Both the mean and the median increase.
The median increases, but the mean does not change.
The mean increases, but the median does not change.
Neither the mean nor the median changes.
questions.explanation: The middle value is still 15, so the median does not change. The sum grows by 15, so the mean rises from $\dfrac{80}{5} = 16$ to $\dfrac{95}{5} = 19$.

questions.skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
questions.prompt: A plant nursery sells seedlings in small trays that hold 12 seedlings each and large trays that hold 30 seedlings each. A farmer bought 18 trays that held a total of 378 seedlings. How many large trays did the farmer buy?
questions.explanation: Let $s$ and $\ell$ be the numbers of small and large trays: $s + \ell = 18$ and $12s + 30\ell = 378$. Substituting $s = 18 - \ell$ gives $216 + 18\ell = 378$, so $\ell = 9$.

questions.prompt: A laboratory culture starts with 500 bacteria, and the number of bacteria doubles every 3 hours. Which function gives the number of bacteria, $N(t)$, $t$ hours after the start?
questions.explanation: The number is multiplied by 2 once every 3 hours, so after $t$ hours it has doubled $\dfrac{t}{3}$ times: $N(t) = 500(2)^{t/3}$. The exponent $3t$ would mean doubling 3 times every hour.

questions.prompt: Each face of a cube is a square, and the total surface area of the cube is 294 square inches. What is the volume of the cube, in cubic inches?
questions.explanation: The 6 faces are equal, so each has area $294 \div 6 = 49$ and each edge is 7. The volume is $7^3 = 343$.

questions.prompt: A seed company tested 300 seeds of two varieties, Red and Gold. The table shows the results. If one of the seeds that germinated is selected at random, what is the probability that it is a Gold seed?
questions.explanation: Only the 240 seeds that germinated count. Of these, 114 are Gold: $\dfrac{114}{240} = \dfrac{19}{40}$. Dividing by the 150 Gold seeds instead gives $\dfrac{19}{25}$, which answers a different question.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A phone plan costs \$12 per month and includes 200 text messages. Each text message beyond the first 200 costs \$0.05. Ethan wants his monthly bill to be at most \$20. What is the greatest total number of text messages he can send in a month?
questions.explanation: Only texts beyond 200 cost extra: $12 + 0.05(t - 200) \le 20$, so $t - 200 \le 160$ and $t \le 360$. 160 is only the number of extra texts.

questions.skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
questions.prompt: Which of the following gives all the solutions to the equation $\sqrt{x + 7} = x - 5$?
questions.explanation: Squaring gives $x + 7 = x^2 - 10x + 25$, or $x^2 - 11x + 18 = 0$, so $x = 2$ or $x = 9$. Check both: for $x = 9$, $\sqrt{16} = 4 = 9 - 5$. For $x = 2$, $\sqrt{9} = 3$ but $2 - 5 = -3$, so 2 is not a solution.

questions.prompt: In right triangle $JKL$, angle $K$ is the right angle, $JL = 26$, and $\sin J = \dfrac{5}{13}$. What is the perimeter of triangle $JKL$?
questions.explanation: $JL$ is the hypotenuse, and the side opposite $J$ is $KL = 26 \cdot \dfrac{5}{13} = 10$. Then $JK = \sqrt{26^2 - 10^2} = 24$, and the perimeter is $10 + 24 + 26 = 60$. 120 is the triangle's area.

questions.prompt: If $(3x - 2)(ax + 5) = 6x^2 + bx - 10$ for all values of $x$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants, what is the value of $b$?
questions.explanation: Matching the $x^2$ terms, $3a = 6$, so $a = 2$. The $x$ terms of $(3x - 2)(2x + 5)$ are $15x - 4x = 11x$, so $b = 11$.

questions.skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
questions.prompt: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of $y = x^2 + 2x - 3$ and the graph of $y = k$, where $k$ is a constant, intersect at exactly one point. What is the value of $k$?
questions.explanation: A horizontal line meets a parabola exactly once only at its vertex. The vertex is at $x = -\dfrac{2}{2} = -1$, where $y = 1 - 2 - 3 = -4$. $-3$ is the $y$-intercept, which the line $y = -3$ crosses at two points.

questions.prompt: A circle has a radius of 6 centimeters. A sector of the circle has an area of $12\pi$ square centimeters. What is the measure, in degrees, of the sector's central angle?
questions.explanation: The whole circle has area $\pi(6)^2 = 36\pi$, so the sector is $\dfrac{12\pi}{36\pi} = \dfrac{1}{3}$ of the circle. Its angle is $\dfrac{1}{3} \times 360 = 120$ degrees.

questions.prompt: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = x^2 + bx + c$, where $b$ and $c$ are constants. The graph of $y = f(x)$ in the $xy$-plane has its vertex at $(3, -4)$. What is the value of $c$?
questions.explanation: With leading coefficient 1 and vertex $(3, -4)$, $f(x) = (x - 3)^2 - 4 = x^2 - 6x + 9 - 4 = x^2 - 6x + 5$, so $c = 5$.

questions.prompt: Line $p$ in the $xy$-plane is parallel to the line $3x - 4y = 12$ and passes through the point $(8, 1)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept of line $p$?
questions.explanation: Solving $3x - 4y = 12$ for $y$ gives $y = \dfrac{3}{4}x - 3$, so line $p$ also has slope $\dfrac{3}{4}$. Then $1 = \dfrac{3}{4}(8) + b$, so $b = -5$. $-3$ is the intercept of the given line, not of line $p$.

questions.prompt: If $42 = 6(x - 2)$, what is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by 6: $7 = x - 2$. Add 2: $x = 9$.

questions.skill: Ratios, rates, proportional relationships, and units
questions.prompt: A car uses 6 liters of fuel to travel 75 kilometers. At this rate, how many liters of fuel will the car use to travel 200 kilometers?
questions.explanation: The car uses $\dfrac{6}{75} = 0.08$ liters per kilometer, and $0.08 \times 200 = 16$.

questions.prompt: The function $p$ is defined by $p(n) = 4 - 3n$. What is the value of $p(2)$?
Which expression is equivalent to $4a + 7b - a + 2b$?
questions.explanation: Combine like terms: $4a - a = 3a$ and $7b + 2b = 9b$.

questions.prompt: The function $k$ is defined by $k(x) = 2x^2 - 1$. What is the value of $k(3)$?
The point $(k, 11)$ lies on the line $y = 3x - 4$ in the $xy$-plane. What is the value of $k$?
questions.explanation: Substitute $y = 11$: $3k - 4 = 11$, so $3k = 15$ and $k = 5$. 29 comes from substituting 11 for $x$ instead of $y$.

questions.prompt: Two angles are supplementary, and one of them measures $68^\circ$. What is the measure of the other angle?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles add up to $180^\circ$: $180 - 68 = 112$. $22^\circ$ would make them complementary (adding to $90^\circ$).

questions.prompt: A rectangle has an area of 84 square meters and a width of 7 meters. What is the length of the rectangle, in meters?
questions.explanation: Area is length times width, so the length is $84 \div 7 = 12$.

questions.skill: One-variable data: distributions and measures of center and spread
questions.prompt: A football team scored the following numbers of goals in its 7 matches this season: $2, 0, 5, 1, 4, 1, 3$. What is the median number of goals per match?
questions.explanation: In order, the values are $0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5$, and the middle (fourth) value is 2. 1 is the middle of the list before it is put in order, and $\dfrac{16}{7}$ is the mean.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: Which of the following values of $n$ is a solution to the inequality $15 - 4n > 3$?
questions.explanation: Subtract 15: $-4n > -12$. Dividing by $-4$ reverses the inequality: $n < 3$. Only 2 is less than 3; $n = 3$ makes the two sides equal.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to $3x(x - 4)$?
questions.explanation: Multiply $3x$ by each term: $3x \cdot x - 3x \cdot 4 = 3x^2 - 12x$.

questions.skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
questions.prompt: $$a = 3b$$ $$2a - b = 35$$ If $(a, b)$ is the solution to the given system of equations, what is the value of $b$?
questions.explanation: Substitute $a = 3b$: $2(3b) - b = 35$, so $5b = 35$ and $b = 7$. 21 is the value of $a$.

questions.prompt: Which expression is equivalent to $9y^2 - 64$?
questions.explanation: This is a difference of squares, $a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)$, with $a = 3y$ and $b = 8$.

questions.skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
questions.prompt: The length of a rectangular tile is 5 centimeters more than its width, and the area of the tile is 36 square centimeters. What is the width of the tile, in centimeters?
questions.explanation: If the width is $w$, then $w(w + 5) = 36$, or $w^2 + 5w - 36 = 0$. Factoring gives $(w + 9)(w - 4) = 0$, and a width must be positive, so $w = 4$.

questions.prompt: Of the 30 students in a class, 18 have visited Paris. If one student from the class is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student has NOT visited Paris?
questions.explanation: $30 - 18 = 12$ students have not visited, so the probability is $\dfrac{12}{30} = \dfrac{2}{5}$. $\dfrac{3}{5}$ is the probability that the student *has* visited.

questions.prompt: A water tank holds 900 liters. When a valve is opened, water drains from the tank at a constant rate of 15 liters per minute. Which function gives the amount of water $W(t)$, in liters, left in the tank $t$ minutes after the valve is opened?
questions.explanation: The tank starts with 900 liters and loses 15 liters each minute, so $W(t) = 900 - 15t$.

questions.prompt: In right triangle $XYZ$, the right angle is at $Y$, $XY = 20$, and $YZ = 15$. What is the value of $\cos X$?
questions.explanation: The hypotenuse is $XZ = \sqrt{20^2 + 15^2} = 25$. The side next to angle $X$ is $XY = 20$, so $\cos X = \dfrac{20}{25} = \dfrac{4}{5}$. $\dfrac{3}{5}$ is $\sin X$.

questions.prompt: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = 2(3)^x$. What is the value of $f(3)$?
questions.explanation: $f(3) = 2 \cdot 3^3 = 2 \cdot 27 = 54$. Multiplying first gives $6^3 = 216$, which ignores the order of operations.

questions.prompt: The line of best fit for a scatterplot is $y = -1.5x + 40$. For what value of $x$ does the line of best fit predict that $y = 25$?
The circumference of a circular pond is $22\pi$ meters. What is the area of the surface of the pond, in square meters?
questions.explanation: $2\pi r = 22\pi$ gives $r = 11$, so the area is $\pi(11)^2 = 121\pi$. $484\pi$ comes from using the diameter, 22, as the radius.

questions.prompt: A gym charges a one-time joining fee of \$40 plus \$25 per month. A member has paid a total of \$315 so far. For how many months has the member paid?
The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = -2(x - 1)^2 + 8$. What is the maximum value of $f(x)$?
questions.explanation: Because $(x - 1)^2 \ge 0$ and it is multiplied by $-2$, the greatest value occurs when $x = 1$: $f(1) = 8$. 1 is the $x$-value where the maximum occurs, and 6 is $f(0)$.

questions.prompt: The sum of three consecutive odd integers is 92 more than the smallest of the three integers. What is the smallest of the three integers?
questions.explanation: Call the integers $n$, $n + 2$, and $n + 4$. Then $3n + 6 = n + 92$, so $2n = 86$ and $n = 43$. (The integers are 43, 45, and 47, whose sum, 135, is 92 more than 43.)

questions.prompt: A store increased the price of a rug by 30%. Later, it decreased the new price by 30%. The final price of the rug was \$273. What was the original price of the rug, in dollars?
questions.explanation: The final price is $1.30 \times 0.70 = 0.91$ times the original, so $0.91p = 273$ and $p = 300$. A 30% increase and a 30% decrease do not cancel out, so 273 is wrong.

questions.prompt: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = ax^2 + 12x + c$, where $a$ and $c$ are constants. The graph of $y = f(x)$ in the $xy$-plane has its maximum at $x = 2$, and $f(2) = 20$. What is the value of $c$?

questions.skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
questions.prompt: $$\dfrac{1}{2}x + 3y = 7$$ $$kx + 12y = 20$$ In the given system of equations, $k$ is a constant. For what value of $k$ does the system have no solution?
questions.explanation: Multiplying the first equation by 4 gives $2x + 12y = 28$. If $k = 2$, the second equation is $2x + 12y = 20$: the same left side with a different right side, so the lines are parallel and never meet. 4 is the multiplier, not the value of $k$.

questions.prompt: The radius of a right circular cylinder is increased by 50%, and its height is decreased by 20%. How does the volume of the new cylinder compare with the volume of the original cylinder?
questions.explanation: Volume is $\pi r^2 h$, so it is multiplied by $1.5^2 \times 0.8 = 2.25 \times 0.8 = 1.8$, an increase of 80%. Adding the percents ($50 - 20 = 30$) ignores that the radius is squared.

questions.skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
questions.prompt: If $x > 0$ and $x^4 - 13x^2 + 36 = 0$, what is the sum of all possible values of $x$?
questions.explanation: Treat it as a quadratic in $x^2$: $(x^2 - 4)(x^2 - 9) = 0$, so $x^2 = 4$ or $x^2 = 9$. With $x > 0$, $x = 2$ or $x = 3$, and $2 + 3 = 5$.

questions.skill: Systems of two linear equations in two variables
questions.prompt: A museum sells adult tickets for \$40 each and student tickets for \$15 each. On one day, it sold 260 tickets for a total of \$7,650. How many student tickets did the museum sell that day?
questions.explanation: Working in dollars: $a + s = 260$ and $40a + 15s = 7{,}650$. Substituting $a = 260 - s$ gives $10{,}400 - 25s = 7{,}650$, so $s = 110$.

questions.prompt: A taxi company charges a fixed starting fare plus a constant amount per kilometer. A 6-kilometer ride costs \$27, and a 10-kilometer ride costs \$39. How much does a 15-kilometer ride cost, in dollars?
questions.explanation: The cost rises by $39 - 27 = 12$ dollars over 4 kilometers, or 3 dollars per kilometer. The starting fare is $27 - 6(3) = 9$ dollars, so 15 kilometers cost $9 + 15(3) = 54$ dollars. Scaling 39 by 1.5 ignores the fixed fare.

questions.prompt: A circle in the $xy$-plane has its center at $(2, 3)$. Line $\ell$ is tangent to the circle at the point $(5, 7)$. What is the slope of line $\ell$?
questions.explanation: The radius to $(5, 7)$ has slope $\dfrac{7 - 3}{5 - 2} = \dfrac{4}{3}$. A tangent line is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, so its slope is $-\dfrac{3}{4}$. $\dfrac{4}{3}$ is the slope of the radius itself.

questions.skill: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables
questions.prompt: $$y = x^2 + 4x + 7$$ $$y = -2x - 2$$ In the $xy$-plane, at how many points do the graphs of the given equations intersect?
questions.explanation: Setting the expressions equal gives $x^2 + 6x + 9 = 0$, or $(x + 3)^2 = 0$. The only solution is $x = -3$ (with $y = 4$), so the line just touches the parabola at one point.

questions.prompt: A bag contains only red tiles and blue tiles. If one tile is drawn at random, the probability that it is red is $\dfrac{3}{8}$. After 10 more red tiles are added to the bag, the probability of drawing a red tile is $\dfrac{1}{2}$. How many tiles were in the bag before the red tiles were added?
questions.explanation: With $n$ tiles at first, there are $\dfrac{3n}{8}$ red ones. Then $\dfrac{3n/8 + 10}{n + 10} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $\dfrac{3n}{4} + 20 = n + 10$ and $n = 40$. 15 is the original number of red tiles, and 50 is the new total.

questions.skill: Linear inequalities in one or two variables
questions.prompt: A farmer has at most 120 hectares of land and at most 4,800 hours of labor for the season. Each hectare of wheat needs 30 hours of labor, and each hectare of cotton needs 60 hours. If the farmer plants $w$ hectares of wheat and $c$ hectares of cotton, which system of inequalities represents these conditions?
questions.explanation: \"At most\" means $\le$. The land used is $w + c$, and the labor used is $30w + 60c$, since wheat takes 30 hours per hectare and cotton takes 60.

questions.prompt: If $\dfrac{1}{x - 2} + \dfrac{3}{x + 2} = \dfrac{ax + b}{x^2 - 4}$ for all $x > 2$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants, what is the value of $a + b$?
questions.explanation: Use the common denominator $(x - 2)(x + 2) = x^2 - 4$: the numerator is $(x + 2) + 3(x - 2) = 4x - 4$. So $a = 4$, $b = -4$, and $a + b = 0$.

questions.prompt: In triangle $ABC$, $AB = AC$. The measure of angle $A$ is $(2x)^\circ$, and the measure of angle $B$ is $(3x + 12)^\circ$. What is the value of $x$?
questions.explanation: Because $AB = AC$, the angles opposite those sides, $B$ and $C$, are equal. So $2x + 2(3x + 12) = 180$, which gives $8x = 156$ and $x = 19.5$. Setting $2x = 3x + 12$ wrongly treats angle $A$ as a base angle.

questions.prompt: The line of best fit for a set of data is $y = 2.4x + 5$. One of the data points is $(6, 17)$. Which statement is true about this data point?
choices: Its $y$-value is 2.4 greater than the value predicted by the line of best fit.
Its $y$-value is 19.4 greater than the value predicted by the line of best fit.
Its $y$-value is equal to the value predicted by the line of best fit.
Its $y$-value is 2.4 less than the value predicted by the line of best fit.
questions.explanation: At $x = 6$, the line predicts $2.4(6) + 5 = 19.4$. The actual value, 17, is $19.4 - 17 = 2.4$ less, so the point lies below the line.

questions.prompt: The function $f$ is defined by $f(x) = x^2 - 4x$. The function $g$ is defined by $g(x) = f(x - 3) + 2$. What is the vertex of the graph of $y = g(x)$ in the $xy$-plane?
questions.explanation: $f(x) = (x - 2)^2 - 4$ has vertex $(2, -4)$. Replacing $x$ with $x - 3$ shifts the graph 3 units right, and adding 2 shifts it 2 units up, giving $(5, -2)$. Shifting left instead gives $(-1, -2)$.

questions.prompt: In right triangle $PQR$, angle $Q$ is the right angle, $\tan P = \dfrac{15}{8}$, and $PQ = 16$. What is the length of $\overline{PR}$?
questions.explanation: $\tan P = \dfrac{QR}{PQ}$, so $QR = 16 \cdot \dfrac{15}{8} = 30$. The hypotenuse is $PR = \sqrt{16^2 + 30^2} = \sqrt{1{,}156} = 34$.

questions.prompt: A line in the $xy$-plane passes through the points $(a, 3)$ and $(5, a)$, where $a$ is a constant, and has a slope of 2. What is the value of $a$?
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{a - 3}{5 - a} = 2$, so $a - 3 = 10 - 2a$, $3a = 13$, and $a = \dfrac{13}{3}$. Subtracting the coordinates in mismatched order ($\dfrac{a - 3}{a - 5}$) gives 7.

questions.skill: Evaluating statistical claims: observational studies and experiments
questions.prompt: Researchers recruited 400 adult volunteers who reported trouble falling asleep. Half of the volunteers, chosen at random, drank a cup of chamomile tea each evening for a month; the others drank a caffeine-free tea that looked and tasted similar but contained no chamomile. On average, the chamomile group fell asleep faster. Which conclusion is best supported by the study?
choices: Drinking chamomile tea likely causes adults with trouble falling asleep, like the volunteers, to fall asleep faster.
Drinking chamomile tea likely causes all adults to fall asleep faster.
Drinking chamomile tea is associated with falling asleep faster, but the study cannot show that it causes faster sleep.
Drinking any kind of tea in the evening likely causes adults to fall asleep faster.
questions.explanation: Random assignment to the two teas supports a cause-and-effect conclusion, so the association-only choice is too weak. But the volunteers were not a random sample of all adults, so the result applies to people like them: adults with trouble falling asleep.

questions.prompt: The function $p$ is defined by $p(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + kx - 10$, where $k$ is a constant. If $x - 2$ is a factor of $p(x)$, what is the value of $k$?
In the equation $\dfrac{1}{2}(8x - 6) = kx + 5$, $k$ is a constant. For what value of $k$ does the equation have no solution?
questions.explanation: The left side is $4x - 3$. If $k = 4$, the equation becomes $4x - 3 = 4x + 5$, or $-3 = 5$, which is never true. For any other $k$, there is exactly one solution. 8 comes from forgetting to multiply by $\dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.prompt: If $2^a = 5$, what is the value of $8^{a + 1}$?
